title: Chapter 33 Quiz — Search Engines: Inverted Indices and BM25

questions.question: An inverted index answers a query without reading every document. What does it store that makes this possible?

options.text: A copy of each document, sorted by its length
For each term, a sorted postings list of the documents that contain it, so a query reads only the lists of its own terms
The similarity between every pair of documents, precomputed
Only the first occurrence of each term in each document

questions.explanation: Lesson 33.1 defines the inverted index as a map from each term to its postings list. A query reads only the lists of its own terms, so when the answer is one document the work does not scale with the whole corpus.

questions.question: Intersect the sorted lists [3, 5, 9] and [1, 5, 7, 9] with the two-pointer AND of Lesson 33.1. What does it return, and how many comparisons does it make?

options.text: [5, 9] after 4 comparisons
[3, 5, 9] after 5 comparisons
[5, 9] after 5 comparisons
[1, 3, 5, 7, 9] after 8 comparisons

questions.explanation: Trace: 3 against 1 advances the second list; 3 against 5 advances the first; 5 equals 5 and is output; 9 against 7 advances the second list; 9 equals 9 and is output. That is five comparisons and the result [5, 9].

questions.question: Encode 300 with VByte, using the convention of Lesson 33.1 in which flag bit 1 means more bytes follow. Which pair of bytes is correct?
questions.explanation: 300 = 2 × 128 + 44. The high group 2 = 0000010 gets flag 1, giving 10000010. The low group 44 = 0101100 gets flag 0, giving 00101100. Option a reverses the groups, option b clears the flag on the high group, and option d reverses the groups and keeps the wrong flags.

questions.question: A term appears in 900 of 1,000 documents. Which statement about its IDF is correct?

options.text: The Robertson–Spärck Jones form gives about −2.19, and the Lucene form gives about 0.106
Both forms give about 0.106
Both forms give about −2.19
Both forms give 0, because the term is common

questions.explanation: Robertson–Spärck Jones (RSJ): log((1000 − 900 + 0.5)/(900 + 0.5)) = log(0.1116) ≈ −2.1928. Lucene: log(1 + 0.1116) ≈ 0.1058. Both values are in the Lesson 33.2 output. A common term does not get IDF 0 under either form.

questions.question: A document has length equal to the average length (avgdl). The query term occurs 3 times, and k1 = 1.2. What is the tf part of the BM25 score?
questions.explanation: With |D| = avgdl the length term is k1, so the tf part is 3 × 2.2 / (3 + 1.2) = 6.6 / 4.2 = 1.5714 (Lesson 33.2). The value 1.0000 is the f = 1 value, 2.2000 is the ceiling k1 + 1 that the tf part approaches but does not reach at f = 3, and 3.0000 is the raw count.

questions.question: In BM25, set the length parameter b to 0. Which statement is correct?

options.text: Longer documents always score lower
Longer documents always score higher
Length matters only when k1 is 0
Length has no effect, because the length term equals k1 for every document

questions.explanation: The length term is k1 (1 − b + b·|D|/avgdl). At b = 0 it reduces to k1 for every document, so the tf part depends only on the count f (Lesson 33.2, Question 2).

questions.question: On the three-document corpus of Lesson 33.3 (lengths 9, 16 and 7), the query 'quick brown fox' has two postings for each term. How many postings entries does the index read, and how many token comparisons does a brute-force scan make?

options.text: 3 postings entries and 32 comparisons
6 postings entries and 96 comparisons
6 postings entries and 32 comparisons
9 postings entries and 96 comparisons

questions.explanation: Three terms with two postings each give 3 × 2 = 6 entries read. The brute-force scan reads every token of every document once per query term: (9 + 16 + 7) × 3 = 96 (Lesson 33.3, Question 4).

questions.question: A colleague calls add() for 1,000 more documents and then calls search() without calling build(). What happens?

options.text: The search runs on the old statistics and returns scores with no error
accumulate() raises an AssertionError with the message 'call build() after the last add()'
The new documents are indexed automatically, so the scores are correct
search() returns an empty list, because the IDF table is cleared

questions.explanation: add() sets built to False, and accumulate() asserts that it is True. Without that check, N, avgdl and the length factors would be stale and the scores wrong, with no error (Lesson 33.3, Common traps and Question 3).
